sections.title: /v1/norms — select the CPRMV namespace with ?cprmv_version=
items: The norms query was hardcoded to the CPRMV 0.3.0 namespace, so data published under any other namespace returned nothing. A new ?cprmv_version= query parameter selects which CPRMV vocabulary version to query and emit; it is validated against the supported set (0.3.0, 0.3.2) and rejects anything else (including 0.4.1) with a 400. It defaults to 0.3.0, preserving existing behaviour.

0.3.0 and 0.3.2 share the flat cprmv:Rule publish shape and differ only in the namespace IRI, so the selected version is threaded through the rules query, the dataset-metadata query (cache now keyed by endpoint + version), the publish-format output keys, the cprmv_version envelope field, and the ETag filter signature — different versions never share a cache entry. The 0.4.1 RuleSet/hasPart model is handled separately and not yet accepted here.

sections.title: Process board ownership — deploy-time tagging
items: Deploy modal now requires a board owner: a new "Board ownership" section auto-detects the board from the process's candidate groups (infra/rip → Infra-board, caseworker/hr → Caseworker) and lets you override it. Deploy is blocked until a board is resolved.

Deployed BPMN is stamped with a process-level camunda:property boardOwner (explicit choice or auto-derived). Injection is idempotent and non-destructive — on any unexpected BPMN shape the original XML is deployed untouched.

boardOwner is persisted on the process_definitions record (new board_owner column) and exposed via /bundles/public, so downstream consumers (ronl-business-api Procesbibliotheek and archive split) can read it.

sections.title: RIP Phase 1 — derive portfolio leadRole
items: The Map role outputs script now sets a leadRole process variable, derived from the intake projectType (contractbeheer → manager-pb, otherwise projectleider). This is the ownership signal the Infra-board Portfolio ROL filter reads.

Distinct from the task candidateGroups: leadRole names who owns the project in the portfolio, not who can claim its tasks. Takes effect for instances started after redeploy; the projectType → leadRole mapping is a placeholder to confirm with the business.

sections.title: CPRMV SHACL — ParameterWaardeShape and TemporalRuleShape
items: Added cprmv:ParameterWaardeShape targeting cprmv:ParameterWaarde: skos:notation [1,1] xsd:string and skos:prefLabel [1,n] rdf:langString are mandatory; schema:value [0,1] xsd:decimal, schema:unitCode [0,1] xsd:string, dct:description [0,1] rdf:langString, and cprmv:validFrom/validUntil [0,1] xsd:date are optional. Previously cprmv:ParameterWaarde had no SHACL shape at all, so the entire Parameters section of an editor-generated TTL was unvalidated.

Added cprmv:TemporalRuleShape targeting cprmv:TemporalRule: cprmv:validFrom [0,1] xsd:date, cprmv:validUntil [0,1] xsd:date, cprmv:confidenceLevel [0,1] xsd:string, and cprmv:isBasedOn [0,n] sh:class cpsv:Rule — all optional. Previously the temporal extensions on cpsv:Rule (validity window, confidence level, extends) were unvalidated by any SHACL shape.
Also adds skos:, schema:, and dct: @prefix declarations required by the new shapes; no changes to existing shapes in the file.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: SHACL Validator: long issue messages and focus-node locations were cut off with an ellipsis and could not be read — the location used a single-line CSS truncate. Messages and locations now wrap in full (break-words / break-all) and expose the complete text on hover (title tooltip).

SHACL backend: removed the 60-character cap on offending values reported for cardinality (maxCount / uniqueLang) violations, so the full value appears in the issue message instead of being truncated with an ellipsis.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: DMNs published under the new CPRMV 0.4.1 namespace (e.g. vast_bedrag_op_vestiging) were missing from /v1/dmns and the ChainBuilder DMN picker — getAllDmns and the chain-link queries only matched cprmv:DecisionModel under the old 0.3.0 namespace. Both namespaces are now supported side by side until existing 0.3.0 data is migrated.

Fixed 'Fill with test data' in the ChainBuilder input form not visibly filling Integer/Double fields when the RDF-sourced test value is 0 — the input rendered as empty (0 || '' = '') instead of showing 0.

sections.title: DSO Integration — deploy-ready DMN + form badge
items: Extracted DSO DMNs now carry camunda:historyTimeToLive, so they deploy to Operaton exactly as handed off — the consumer no longer has to patch the DMN before deploying. LDE now produces a fully deploy-ready and evaluatable DMN (DMN 1.3, input ids, FEEL-safe variable names, output typeRefs, history TTL).
Forms imported from DSO now show a green DSO badge in the Form Editor list, instead of the generic yellow WIP badge.

sections.title: SHACL Validator — CPRMV layer + validation test fixtures
items: The SHACL validator now checks uploaded Turtle against a CPRMV 0.4.1 shape layer alongside CPSV-AP 3.2.0 and the RONL Custom rules; the results panel renders the new layer automatically.

Added valid/invalid test fixtures for every layer — CPRMV (cprmv-conformant.ttl / cprmv-nonconformant.ttl), CPSV-AP (cpsv-ap-conformant.ttl / cpsv-ap-rule-nonconformant.ttl), and RONL (rule- and org-collision pass/fail) — plus a malformed-Turtle case covering the parser path.

sections.title: DSO Integration — Phase 2d + 4.2
items: Activities tab now supports name search: fixing a location (Lelystad / Flevoland) loads that authority's full activity set in one call and reveals a search box that live-filters by name, so activities like 'Boom kappen of houtopstand vellen' are findable without walking the hierarchy.

↓ Import into LDE button (Indieningsvereisten only) saves the generated form-js scaffold straight into the Form Editor as a draft, named after the activity and tagged with the authority — no manual download/import step needed.
Imported forms are now tagged with the readable authority name (e.g. 'Lelystad') instead of the bare RTR code (GM0995), falling back to the code for authorities outside the known presets.

sections.title: DSO Integration — DMN publish handoff (Phase 4.1)
items: Publish via CPSV Editor button (Conclusie only) opens the CPSV Editor with a deep-link to publish the extracted DMN to TriplyDB, where the LDE DMN picker can consume it — no local DMN store needed.

Extracted DMNs are now normalized to deploy and evaluate on Operaton: DMN 1.2 is upgraded to 1.3, missing input ids are added, variable names are made FEEL-safe (hyphens/spaces broke evaluation), and output columns get an explicit typeRef.
Verified end-to-end against Operaton: the normalized HoutopstandVellen decision deploys (all 7 decisions) and the root decision evaluates without the previous FEEL error.

sections.title: DSO Integration — Phase 2a + 4
items: Activity Detail panel now shows an 'Applicable Rules' section listing toepasbare regels fetched live from the DSO Uitvoeren Gegevens API, grouped by rule type (Conclusie / Indieningsvereisten) with validity date and STTR version.
↓ STTR button downloads the raw STTR XML for any rule type.
↓ Extract DMN button (Conclusie only) extracts the embedded DMN decision table as a standalone .dmn file ready for import into LDE or deployment to Operaton.

↓ Form scaffold button (Indieningsvereisten only) generates a form-js JSON scaffold from the STTR questionnaire, mapping boolean questions to checkboxes, list questions to select fields with options, number questions to number fields, and attachment requirements to labelled textfields.
Added ronl:dsoActiviteitUrn extension on TreeFellingPermitSubProcess linking it to nl.imow-gm0995.activiteit.HoutopstandVellen (Gemeente Lelystad).

sections.title: BPMN Modeler
items: Uploaded BPMN processes that form a shell/subprocess pair are now automatically linked: a process with call-activity elements is classified as a shell, and any process whose BPMN process ID is targeted by a shell's call-activity is classified as its subprocess. The relationship is detected both on fresh imports and retroactively on startup, so previously uploaded standalone processes are reclassified without requiring a re-upload.
Removed two unused TypeScript imports (DsoWerkzaamheid, zoekActiviteiten) in DsoExplorer.

sections.title: SHACL Validator
items: Vendored the canonical CPSV-AP 3.2.0 SHACL shapes (SEMIC) — the CPSV-AP layer is now active, validating the full model (PublicService, Rule, PublicOrganisation, ContactPoint, Channel, Address, …) across 32 shapes. Previously this layer reported no shapes.
Collapsed the earlier CPSV-AP Core and CPSV-AP Vocabularies layers into a single CPSV-AP 3.2.0 layer, matching SEMIC's combined shape file for the 3.2.0 release.
Layer results now distinguish 'Not loaded' (no shapes present for that layer) from 'OK' (evaluated and clean), so an unvendored layer no longer shows a misleading green check.
Offending values listed in cardinality and uniqueLang messages are now whitespace-normalised and capped at 60 characters, keeping long published descriptions readable.
Added a fully CPSV-AP-conformant example plus deterministic merge-simulated test coverage (a cross-publication homepage collision), alongside the existing file-local fixtures.

sections.title: SHACL Validator
items: New SHACL Validator view in the sidebar: drop one or more CPSV-AP Turtle (.ttl) files and validate them against the bundled CPSV-AP 3.2.0 and RONL SHACL shapes before publishing. Results reuse the DMN Validator's layered layout, grouped into CPSV-AP Core, CPSV-AP Vocabularies, and RONL Custom with per-layer error/warning/info counts.

Two backend endpoints under a new Validation route category: POST /v1/shacl/validate (file-local) and POST /v1/shacl/validate-merged. Both return the same { valid, parseError, layers, summary } shape as /v1/dmns/validate, so the frontend renders them with the existing components.

Merge-simulated mode unions the uploaded file with the triples already published for its subjects — fetched from the configured SPARQL endpoint via a standard SPARQL 1.1 CONSTRUCT with one level of blank-node closure — then validates the union. This catches fan-out against live data that a file-local check cannot see; an optional endpoint field overrides the server default.

RONL shape PublicOrganisationUniquenessShape: at most one foaf:homepage, dct:identifier and cv:spatial per cv:PublicOrganisation, plus sh:uniqueLang on skos:prefLabel. Flags the duplicate-homepage fan-out where one organisation URI ends up with both a www. and non-www. homepage across publications.

RONL shape RuleUniquenessShape: sh:uniqueLang on dct:title and dct:description for cpsv:Rule. Detects subject-URI collisions where several distinct rules were authored under one URI and merge into N titles × M descriptions of duplicate rows in SPARQL results, while tolerating legitimate bilingual (nl/en) labels.
Cardinality and uniqueLang violations list the offending values inline (whitespace-normalised and capped at 60 characters) so collisions are immediately identifiable.

sections.title: New Features
items: Download the deployed DMN XML directly from Operaton via the new GET /v1/dmns/:identifier/xml endpoint — the file is streamed as <identifier>.dmn with the correct Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers so browsers save it automatically.
DMN list and detail responses now include an xmlUrl field pointing to the new download endpoint, making the link self-discoverable for API clients without prior knowledge of the URL pattern.
Backward compatible: the legacy GET /api/dmns/:definitionKey/xml route remains available for existing consumers.

sections.title: DMN validator: INT-007 false positives eliminated
items: INT-007 (Interaction Rules layer) no longer flags valid intra-DRD references. An <inputExpression> may legitimately reference a value produced by another decision wired in via <informationRequirement><requiredDecision> — that name is the producing decision's <variable name> or <decisionTable>/<output name>, never an <inputData>. The rule now resolves requiredDecision targets and treats their output variables as satisfied, mirroring the requiredInput → inputData resolution INT-001 already performs.

INT-007 now parses FEEL expressions instead of whole-text matching. Previously the entire <inputExpression><text> was treated as one variable name, so date and time(aanvraagDatum) demanded an <inputData name="date and time(aanvraagDatum)"> and any operator expression false-fired. A new shared extractFeelIdentifiers() helper strips string literals, unwraps built-in calls (date(...), date and time(...), number(...), string(...), not(...), …), drops FEEL keywords/operators and qualified-name/property segments after a dot, and extracts each referenced identifier — every identifier is checked individually.

Decision outputs are excluded from the input-contract check entirely. Output variable names (decision <variable> and decision-table <output name>) are, by construction, never external inputs and are no longer subject to the must-have-matching-inputData requirement.

Genuine gaps still flagged: an inputExpression identifier that resolves to neither a declared <inputData> nor a requiredDecision-produced output continues to raise INT-007, now naming the specific identifier rather than the raw expression string.

Verified against real DMNs that deploy and evaluate correctly on Operaton: RONL_Heusden_Heusdenpas.dmn (aanmerkingHeusdenPas consumed purely via requiredDecision), RONL_SVB_Leeftijden.dmn (date(dagVanAanvraag).year property access), EmployeeRoleAssignment.dmn, tree-felling-decision.dmn and replacement-tree-decision.dmn all validate clean; backend tsc --noEmit passes.
No API or response-shape change. POST /v1/dmns/validate is unchanged; only the interaction-layer issue set for affected files differs (fewer false-positive warnings).

sections.title: Concurrent applicable periods per ruleset on /v1/norms
items: A single BWB ruleset can have multiple cprmv:Dataset records — different applicable periods of the same law (e.g. the 2025-01-01 and 2026-01-01 editions of the Participatiewet) are concurrent and equally authoritative, not competing versions. The v1.7 design hid all but the latest; v1.8 surfaces them all.

Breaking shape change: dataset_versions[<rulesetid>] is now a list of { version, published_at, title } records, not a single object. Replaces v1.7.0 (which was never used externally — API stability contract hadn't been promised at that release).
List is pre-sorted: version descending with nulls at the end, ties broken by published_at descending. Element [0] is the most-recent applicable version of that ruleset.
SPARQL query simplified: dropped the FILTER NOT EXISTS subpattern and now fetches all cprmv:Dataset records. Grouping and sort live in the service layer.

sections.title: Cache header semantics preserved across the shape change
items: ETag now hashes every (version, published_at) pair in dataset_versions — a new applicable period being added to any ruleset changes the ETag
Last-Modified is max(published_at) across all records in the response (not just the first per ruleset)
Cache-Control semantics unchanged: full headers when every rulesetid has metadata; no-cache otherwise

sections.title: Graph-name traceability on /v1/triplydb/update-service
items: New optional graphName field in the POST /v1/triplydb/update-service request body — accepts the IRI of the graph that triggered the sync (e.g. https://regels.overheid.nl/graphs/Sociale_Verzekeringsbank/aow-leeftijd); requests that omit it continue to work unchanged

graphName threaded through to the route logger as graphName and to the service logger as triggeredByGraph — multi-publish flows landing in distinct per-service graphs are now traceable end-to-end without inspecting TriplyDB internals

updateService() in packages/backend/src/services/triplydb.service.ts extended with a fourth optional parameter graphName?: string; existing graphNames?: string[] parameter unchanged for backward compatibility
Response envelope from /v1/triplydb/update-service now echoes graphName when it was supplied in the request, omitted otherwise — additive shape change with no breaking impact on existing clients

The underlying TriplyDB sync call (POST /datasets/{account}/{dataset}/services/{serviceName} with body {"sync":"true"}) is unchanged — graphName is purely observability metadata, since the TriplyDB sync endpoint has no graph-scoping mechanism of its own

sections.title: Per-rulesetid dataset versioning on /v1/norms
items: New envelope field: dataset_versions — a per-rulesetid map keyed by cprmv:rulesetId, each entry carrying { version, published_at } for the latest cprmv:Dataset record of that ruleset

Each BWB ruleset (BWBR0002471, BWBR0004044, ...) is published as a distinct cprmv:Dataset resource in TriplyDB, on its own publication cadence; a single /v1/norms response can span multiple rulesets at different versions
Backend picks the latest cprmv:Dataset per cprmv:rulesetId via a FILTER NOT EXISTS subpattern — historical versions remain queryable in TriplyDB but consumers see only the latest
New envelope field: cprmv_version — backend constant extracted from the CPRMV namespace URI, describes which vocabulary the backend speaks independently of which data is published
Internal 60-second cache on the dataset metadata SPARQL query — biannual data tolerates this happily and keeps the metadata lookup off the hot path

sections.title: HTTP cache headers for G2G consumers
items: ETag header: opaque 8-hex strong validator hashed over the sorted dataset_versions map plus all request parameters affecting the response shape

Last-Modified header: max(published_at) across the response's datasets in RFC 7231 format — If-Modified-Since returns 304 only when nothing in the consumer's query has been republished since their last fetch
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 set only when every rulesetid in the response has dataset metadata; falls back to no-cache otherwise

Safe-by-default partial-coverage policy: if any rulesetid in the response is missing a cprmv:Dataset record, all three cache headers degrade to no-cache so consumers can't be misled into serving stale data for an unversioned ruleset
Single-rulesetid queries get a fast 304 path: the cheap (cached) metadata lookup decides freshness BEFORE the expensive rules SPARQL query runs
New utility module packages/backend/src/utils/etag.ts with computeNormsEtag() and computeLastModified(): key-order-independent and undefined-tolerant serialisation

sections.title: API stability contract published
items: New IOU documentation page at /linked-data-explorer/reference/api-stability — binding contract for G2G consumers covering the four versioning layers, PK semantics, additive evolution promise, per-rulesetid publication detection, partial-coverage behaviour, breaking-change criteria, and 24-month deprecation policy when v2 eventually arrives
Documents the immutability guarantee for the (rulesetid, applicable_date, rulesetid_index) tuple as the eternal primary key — consumers can cache permanently and never invalidate
Documents the rule_id_path_key field as the logical identifier for querying 'the current value of this rule' across its lifetime
Documents the cprmv:Dataset publication model: each BWB ruleset is a distinct dataset on its own cadence; rollout is from scratch with no retroactive backfill of existing rulesets
Quick-reference table at the bottom covering the questions a new G2G consumer is most likely to ask first

sections.title: Stable keys and version indices on /v1/norms
items: New rule_id_path_key field: rule_id_path with the date and index segments removed, e.g. "BWBR0002471_2025-01-01_0, Artikel 2, lid 6" → "BWBR0002471, Artikel 2, lid 6"; stable across versions of the same ruleset, suitable as a deduplication key when aggregating norms across applicable_date values
New rulesetid_index field: the integer index segment after the date in rule_id_path (e.g. the _0 in BWBR..._2025-01-01_0); distinguishes multiple versions published on the same date

Both new fields, together with applicable_date, are derived from a single regex pass over rule_id_path; all three emit JSON null when the path does not match the canonical <rulesetid>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<index>[, <rest>] shape
Key insertion order extended: rulesetid, applicable_date, rulesetid_index, rule_id_path, rule_id_path_key — identifier metadata grouped first, then the path and its derived stable key together

sections.title: Per-rulesetid aggregation
items: Response envelope now carries an aggregations.norms_per_rulesetid map alongside rules, listing the count of top-level rules per cprmv:rulesetId in the filtered result set
Counts are keyed by the authoritative cprmv:rulesetId value (not parsed from the path), so non-conforming rule_id_path values still aggregate correctly
Sum of values equals data.total, letting clients render ruleset-level summaries without a second pass over rules
Additive change — existing readers of data.rules and data.total see no breaking change

sections.title: Single source of truth for v1 routes
items: New backend module packages/backend/src/routes/registry.ts: every v1 route's mount path, router, summary and category lives in one array; adding a route is a one-line entry that both registration and the root page pick up automatically

Refactored packages/backend/src/routes/index.ts to iterate the registry for v1 mounting; legacy /api/* deprecation aliases stay hand-mounted (deprecated routes are intentionally excluded from the registry to steer consumers towards /v1/*)
Mount-order semantics preserved: more specific paths still precede their parents (/v1/chains/templates before /v1/chains) so Express route precedence behaves exactly as before

sections.title: Content-negotiated root page
items: GET / now serves HTML when Accept includes text/html (browsers) and JSON otherwise (curl, fetch with default Accept, programmatic pollers); both views are derived from the shared route registry so they cannot drift
HTML view groups endpoints by category (Health & monitoring, Discovery, Execution, Assets, Integrations) and badges public-CORS endpoints; styling is inline with no external dependencies

JSON payload preserves backwards compatibility: same top-level keys as before (name, version, environment, status, documentation, health, endpoints, legacy); existing programmatic clients see no breaking change
Closes the drift gap that was missing /v1/dso, /v1/norms, /v1/assets/*, /v1/cache, /v1/edocs, /v1/ropa, /v1/process and /v1/chains/templates from the previous hand-coded listing

sections.title: Deployment tier display label
items: New DEPLOYMENT_ENV environment variable distinguishes ACC from PROD when NODE_ENV is 'production' for both; falls back to NODE_ENV when unset so local development needs no change

Added config.displayEnv (string) and config.deploymentEnv (raw value) to packages/backend/src/utils/config.ts with mappings: prod/production → PROD, acc/acceptance/staging → ACC, dev/development/local → development, test → test, unknown values pass through
Used consistently by the HTML root page and the /v1/health response so the displayed environment stays in sync across surfaces
Configuration is per Azure App Service: az webapp config appsettings set ... --settings DEPLOYMENT_ENV=acc (or prod)

sections.title: New /v1/norms endpoint
items: New backend route GET /v1/norms exposing all cprmv:Rule paths and norms in the publish format consumed by the SPARQL editor's norm publisher
Response mirrors the cprmv-example.json shape exactly: fully-qualified RDF/CPRMV keys for type/id/definition/contains, short keys for situatie/norm/per/rulesetid/applicable_date/rule_id_path
Parent rules and their cprmv:contains children are aggregated into nested objects in a single response, with deterministic key ordering preserved across runs
Optional ?endpoint= query parameter overrides the default TriplyDB endpoint, matching the pattern already used by /v1/dmns

sections.title: Filtering by ruleset and applicable date
items: New applicable_date attribute derived from the _YYYY-MM-DD_ segment embedded in rule_id_path; null when no date is present in the path
Filter by ?rulesetid= (e.g. BWBR0015703) and/or ?applicable_date= (e.g. 2026-01-01); both parameters can be combined
Strict input validation against /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ (rulesetid) and /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ (applicable_date) returns 400 INVALID_PARAM before any SPARQL fires
Validated filters are applied as SPARQL FILTER clauses (exact-match on rulesetId, CONTAINS on the dated segment of ruleIdPath) for server-side selection

sections.title: Maintenance
items: Silenced TypeScript 5.x deprecation warning on moduleResolution: "node10" via "ignoreDeprecations": "6.0" in packages/backend/tsconfig.json; full migration to nodenext deferred until ESM-on-Node maturity warrants the per-file .js extension changes

sections.title: Multilingualism — new
items: Language metadata on BPMN, Form, and Document artefacts (ISO 639-1: en, nl, de) — set via the editor footer panel; persisted to PostgreSQL and to BPMN XML as ronl:language; round-trips through export and import
Organization metadata on the same three artefact types — set via the editor footer with autocomplete from existing organizations; drives list-panel grouping
Language filter and free-text search across all three list panels (Processes, Forms, Documents)
Collapsible organization groups in all three list panels — subprocesses follow their shell's organization regardless of their own tag; orphan subprocesses (shell hidden by filter) render flat

Filename-based language inference on import — drop a capacity-claim-intake.nl.form into the form import and the language tag is applied automatically; XML and JSON wrapper values take precedence over filename inference
Form export now includes language and organization at the top of the JSON, plus a language-suffixed filename — round-trip integrity for all three artefact types
Deploy-time language consistency check — amber warning surfaces inline in the deploy modal when a bundle mixes languages, listing the offending codes; same UX as the existing RoPA-missing warning

sections.title: HR-capacity Dutch reference bundle — new
items: Beheer capaciteitsclaim — proces (Voorbeeld, NL): 1 BPMN, 8 forms, 2 documents, all tagged language=nl, organization=flevoland
Demonstrates stable English DMN keys with translated form labels — the same CapacityClaimRouting DMN serves both the English and Dutch siblings without duplication

All formRef and documentRef values in the Dutch BPMN suffixed -nl; flow labels (formatie, inhuur, akkoord, afgewezen, doorgaan, intrekken, werving, inkoop) translated; gateway condition expressions unchanged

sections.title: Pending-until-Save editing model
items: Footer edits across BPMN, Forms, and Documents (language, organization, RoPA, DSO activiteit) no longer persist immediately — they accumulate in a draft and flush atomically on Save
Navigation guard with confirm prompt when leaving an artefact with unsaved changes (Create / Load another / Close)

Shell → subprocess atomic save — saving a shell propagates language and organization to all linked subprocesses in one write; idempotent (skips subprocesses already aligned); shell wins unconditionally
Save buttons now correctly reflect dirty state — Form Save was previously always-enabled (regression); now disables on load and after Save, enables on first edit

sections.title: Bug fixes
items: BPMN persistence: language and organization fields are now included in the BpmnService POST payload — previously dropped silently on the API call, causing values to vanish on hydration

OrganizationSelector input is now controlled (value/onChange) rather than uncontrolled (defaultValue/onBlur) — switching between artefacts now refreshes the input correctly; previous value no longer leaks across selections
BpmnCanvas no longer resets on every parent re-render — handleElementSelect stabilized via a ref, modeler-init effect deps narrowed to xml only

DocumentComposer no longer flips hasChanges spuriously on document load — TipTap and other child editors emit synthetic onUpdate events during mount that previously dirtied the parent; a load-window guard now suppresses those for the macrotask following load

sections.title: Backend & technical
items: Database — language VARCHAR(2) and organization VARCHAR(100) columns added to process_definitions, form_schemas, and document_templates with partial indexes; nullable, existing rows coexist as NULL
BPMN moddle descriptor extended with LanguageMixin and OrganizationMixin on bpmn:Process — custom attributes survive saveXML round-trip via the existing ronl namespace
New shared components under packages/frontend/src/components/common/: LanguageSelector, OrganizationSelector, ArtefactListToolbar (with filterArtefacts helper)

Editor architecture — footer state lifted to the editor parent (BpmnModeler / FormEditor / DocumentComposer); children receive effective values via props and report changes via callbacks; Save is the single point of persistence

EXAMPLE_VERSIONS bumped for all existing examples to trigger one-time re-seed with organization tags; eleven new HR-capacity Dutch entries added at v1; organization keys standardized to lowercase (flevoland, toeslagen, bzk)

sections.title: Known limitations
items: form-js properties panel loses input focus when typing pauses (Field label, Description, Key) — upstream form-js issue #86, marked wontfix by bpmn-io; not LDE-caused, not fixable from React without forking form-js; workaround: edit .form JSON in a code editor and re-import — filename inference handles language tagging on import

sections.title: Works tab — new
items: New Works tab in the DSO Explorer (between Concepts and Activities) backed by the Zoekinterface API — search werkzaamheden by user intent (e.g. 'boom kappen') with autocomplete suggestions after 2 characters
Each result shows the human-readable omschrijving, the functioneleStructuurRef (full concept URI — the Phase 4 pivot to STTR files), and the short werkzaamheid URN
Selecting a result opens a detail panel showing the current version's omschrijving, validity period, and full version history with start/end dates and a 'current' badge
Autocomplete uses POST /werkzaamheden/_suggereer with 300ms debounce; selecting a suggestion immediately fires the search
Reloads on DSO environment switch with the same clean-slate behaviour as the other tabs

sections.title: Activities tab — OIN preset fix
items: Lelystad and Flevoland presets now use POST /activiteiten/_zoek with bestuursorgaan.oin filter instead of _wijzigingen — returns activities valid on a given date rather than a delta sync of changed activities
Activities now appear in the list with their full omschrijving visible immediately, without requiring parallel detail fetches
Date field now defaults to today for OIN presets (yesterday offset removed — no longer needed with _zoek)
Pagination works correctly in OIN mode — Load button reloads the authority list for the selected date
Empty state message distinguishes between no activities found in general vs no activities found for the selected authority on the selected date

sections.title: Bug fixes
items: Fixed Activity Detail panel always using pre-production DSO when opened from the Activities list — env was missing from the getActiviteitDetail call, causing 404 for production-only activities
Fixed Activity Detail panel not re-fetching when DSO environment is switched while a URN is already selected — env added to the useEffect dependency array
Fixed Activity Detail panel showing stale date context in OIN preset mode — activeDatum now set correctly by loadByOin alongside the result

Fixed _wijzigingen datumVanaf returning empty for dates within the last two weeks — root cause was that _wijzigingen is a delta sync endpoint, not a browse endpoint; replaced entirely with _zoek + OIN filter

sections.title: Backend — DSO service
items: zoekinterfaceBaseUrl and opvragenWerkzaamhedenBaseUrl added to both dso and dsoProd config blocks — defaults baked in, no new env vars required
POST /v1/dso/werkzaamheden/zoek — proxies Zoekinterface /werkzaamheden/_zoek
POST /v1/dso/werkzaamheden/suggereer — proxies Zoekinterface /werkzaamheden/_suggereer
GET /v1/dso/werkzaamheden/:urn — proxies Opvragen Werkzaamheden /werkzaamheden/{urn} (version history, without expand — _expandScope enum value not yet resolved)

sections.title: DSO Explorer — improvements
items: DSO environment selector added to the Settings panel (gear icon): switch between pre-production and production DSO independently of the LDE environment, persisted across sessions in localStorage
Environment badge in the DSO Explorer header updates to reflect the active DSO environment (amber for pre-production, green for production)
Both DSO environments (pre-production and production) use separate API keys configured via DSO_API_KEY and DSO_API_KEY_PROD environment variables

Location presets (Lelystad, Flevoland) now filter by authority OIN via POST /activiteiten/_wijzigingen instead of geometry — shows only that authority's registered activities rather than all activities geographically intersecting the area
datumVanaf flows from the Valid on date field through to the _wijzigingen call — changing the date while a preset is active and pressing Load reloads that authority's list for the new date
Pressing Load while a preset is active reloads the authority list for the selected date instead of deselecting the preset and reverting to the default list
Clear button added next to active preset label to explicitly reset to the default list
Yesterday used as the default datumVanaf for authority presets
Child activities in the detail panel now show human-readable names fetched in parallel after the parent detail loads
Graceful 404 handling in the detail panel: activities not available in the active DSO environment show a clear message instead of a raw error
Pagination unified to 20 items per page across both Concepts and Activities tabs

sections.title: Backend — DSO service
items: POST /v1/dso/activiteiten/oin — new endpoint wrapping _wijzigingen, accepts oin and optional datumVanaf, defaults to yesterday
X-Dso-Env request header added to all DSO frontend calls; backend reads it to select pre-production or production DSO config
X-Dso-Env added to CORS allowedHeaders to resolve preflight errors
dsoProd config block in config.ts: DSO_CATALOGUE_BASE_URL_PROD, DSO_RTR_BASE_URL_PROD, DSO_API_KEY_PROD environment variables
getDsoConfig() helper selects the correct base URL and API key per request
env parameter threaded through all dso.service.ts exported functions and logged with each DSO request

Activities without an omschrijving in DSO gracefully fall back to their URN in both the list and the detail panel child links

sections.title: DSO Explorer
items: New DSO Explorer panel (Landmark icon in sidebar) connecting LDE to the Digitaal Stelsel Omgevingswet pre-production environment
Concepts tab: full-text search across the Stelselcatalogus /begrippen endpoint — returns definitions, explanations, validity dates, and concept URIs
Activities tab: paginated list of RTR activiteiten valid on any selected date, defaulting to today with manual dd-MM-yyyy formatting (Azure App Service Intl-safe)
Location presets for Lelystad and Flevoland filter the activity list via POST /activiteiten/_zoek with GeoJSON Point geometry
URN paste-to-inspect input: paste any activiteit URN directly to open its detail panel without navigating the list

Activity Detail panel (1/3 width): shows omschrijving, authority (bestuurslaag, organisatieType, organisatieCode, OIN), parent activity, validity window, refinable flag, rule types present (conclusie / indieningsvereisten / maatregelen), child activities, and location identifiers
Parent and child activity links are navigable — clicking navigates the detail panel without returning to the list
DSO Explorer header shows environment label (pre-production) to make the data context explicit

sections.title: DSO ↔ BPMN Linking
items: New ronl:dsoActiviteitUrn moddleExtension on bpmn:Process — persisted in the BPMN XML alongside ronl:ropaRef
DsoActiviteitSelector footer panel in the BPMN Modeler (below RopaSelector): paste a URN, verify it live against the DSO RTR, and save it to the active process
Verification call fetches the activity detail and confirms omschrijving and authority before saving — prevents storing invalid URNs
Direct link to the activity in the production RTR viewer (omgevingswet.overheid.nl) shown after successful verification
TreeFellingPermitSubProcess can now be formally grounded in its DSO activiteit (boom kappen / nl.imow-gm0014) as the first Phase 3 example

sections.title: Backend — DSO Service
items: New dso.service.ts with shared dsoFetch helper: x-api-key header, configurable timeout, clean error propagation
GET /v1/dso/begrippen — proxies Catalogus /begrippen with zoekTerm, geldigOp, page, pageSize forwarding
GET /v1/dso/activiteiten — proxies RTR /activiteiten with today-default datum (manual dd-MM-yyyy format, no Intl dependency)
GET /v1/dso/activiteiten/:urn — fetches a single activity by URN with today-default datum
POST /v1/dso/activiteiten/zoek — proxies RTR /activiteiten/_zoek with GeoJSON geometrie body and crs=epsg:4326 query param
DSO config block in config.ts: DSO_CATALOGUE_BASE_URL, DSO_RTR_BASE_URL, DSO_API_KEY, DSO_TIMEOUT environment variables

sections.title: Public Bundle Library
items: New public endpoint GET /v1/bundles/public serves deployed bundle records with no authentication required and fully open CORS — consumable by the RONL Business API caseworker dashboard
A bundle is recorded at deploy time: shell or standalone BPMN process, Operaton deployment ID, Operaton URL, resolved form IDs, and resolved document template IDs are written to process_definitions
Forms and documents are expanded by name in the response — forms joined via schema JSON id field, documents joined via document_templates.id
Subprocesses linked to a shell via calledElement are resolved and included as a nested array
New PATCH /v1/assets/bpmn/:id/deploy endpoint writes deployment metadata back to the process_definitions row immediately after a successful Operaton deploy
To cover example bundles removed `readonly: true` from the seed records entirely, kept the EXAMPLE badge, and protect deletion by checking status === 'example' instead of readonly
PATCH method added to the backend CORS allowed methods list

sections.title: Deploy Write-back
items: BpmnCanvas fires a background PATCH to /v1/assets/bpmn/:id/deploy after every successful deploy — no spinner, no blocking UX change
Write-back carries: Operaton deployment ID, Operaton URL, form IDs resolved from camunda:formRef, document IDs resolved from ronl:documentRef
LDE process ID is resolved by matching the active process bpmnProcessId against the deployment processKey — only user-authored (non-readonly) processes are written
Redeploying a bundle updates the existing row — deployed_at is always the most recent successful deploy

sections.title: RoPA Records — PostgreSQL
items: Two new PostgreSQL tables: ropa_records (one record per process) and ropa_personal_data_fields (one row per personal data field collected by the linked forms)
ropa_records keyed by bpmn_process_id with a unique index — re-running the seed updates records in place rather than inserting duplicates
ropa_personal_data_fields cascade-deleted when the parent record is removed, ensuring referential integrity
New backend service ropa.service.ts with transactional upsert: record header and all field rows committed atomically or rolled back together
Seeded with four active records covering the AWB Shell (Flevoland), Tree Felling Permit subprocess, AWB Shell (Zorgtoeslag), and Zorgtoeslag Provisional Entitlement subprocess

sections.title: RoPA Records — API
items: Authenticated asset routes: GET/POST /v1/assets/ropa and DELETE /v1/assets/ropa/:id, GET /v1/assets/ropa/by-bpmn-id/:bpmnProcessId
Public read-only route GET /v1/ropa/public?organisation= with open CORS — serves only active records and strips internal contact details before returning
Public route bypasses the global CORS origin whitelist via path-aware middleware in index.ts, enabling consumption from any external domain including ropa.flevoland.nl

sections.title: RoPA Editor — LDE UI
items: New RoPA Records view in the LDE sidebar (ScrollText icon), using the same three-panel layout as BPMN Modeler and Document Composer
Left panel: record list grouped as shells first then subprocesses, with DRAFT / ACTIVE / ARCHIVED status badges and delete controls
Record tab: all GDPR Art. 30 mandatory fields — controller, purpose, GDPR article, legal basis, data subjects, recipients, third-country transfers, retention period, security measures
Legal basis Lookup button queries the TriplyDB SPARQL endpoint for eli:LegalResource resources and presents a pick-list — selected URI and label populate both fields automatically
Personal Data Fields tab: hydrates field rows from the form schemas linked to the process via camunda:formRef — Product Owner classifies each field with a data category and Art. 9/10 flag
BPMN Link tab: reads and writes ronl:ropaRef directly into the process XML via BpmnService, with status indicator showing whether the current record ID matches the value in the BPMN
Status tab: three lifecycle buttons (Draft / Active / Archived) with confirmation dialog before activation — activating a record makes it publicly visible

sections.title: RoPA Selector — BPMN Modeler
items: RoPA record selector rendered as a fixed footer panel at the bottom of the ProcessList when a process is active — no canvas element selection required
Selecting a record writes ronl:ropaRef into the process XML and persists via BpmnService.saveProcess, including automatic xmlns:ronl namespace injection if absent
ronl:ropaRef added to ronlModdleDescriptor.json as a bpmn:Process-level attribute alongside the existing ronl:documentRef UserTask extension
Deploy modal shows an amber warning when no ronl:ropaRef is found on the process element — non-blocking but visible before production deployment

sections.title: RoPA Public Site — MVP
items: New package packages/ropa-site — a zero-dependency static HTML/CSS/JS site deployable as an Azure Static Web Apps resource isolated from the LDE stack
Fetches active RoPA records from GET /v1/ropa/public and renders them as collapsible cards with Provincie Flevoland house style (dark green accent)
Each card shows controller, GDPR article, legal basis (linked to eli:LegalResource URI), purpose, data subjects, recipients, retention period, security measures, and a personal data fields table
Personal data fields table colour-codes data categories and flags Art. 9/10 special categories in red
Shells rendered first, subprocesses second — matching the AWB two-level process hierarchy
staticwebapp.config.json included for Azure Static Web Apps deployment with no-cache headers

sections.title: PostgreSQL Asset Storage
items: BPMN processes, form schemas, and document templates now persist to PostgreSQL via the LDE backend — assets survive localStorage clearing and are shared across browsers and devices
Write-through cache strategy: saves update localStorage immediately for zero-latency UI, then POST to /v1/assets/ in the background
Async hydration on editor mount: GET /v1/assets/ replaces non-readonly localStorage entries with authoritative server state on each page load
Graceful degradation: if the backend is unreachable, localStorage is used as fallback without any error surfaced to the user
Example assets (readonly: true) are excluded from server writes — they remain seeded from public/examples/ as before
New backend routes: GET/POST /v1/assets/bpmn, GET/POST /v1/assets/forms, GET/POST /v1/assets/documents, DELETE /v1/assets/{type}/:id
New backend route GET /v1/assets/bpmn/by-bpmn-id/:bpmnProcessId for bundle assembly lookup by BPMN process id

sections.title: AWB Shell / Subprocess Hierarchy
items: BpmnProcess type extended with bpmnProcessId, processRole ('shell' | 'subprocess' | 'standalone'), and calledElement fields

All seeded example processes carry explicit role and relationship metadata: AwbShellProcess and AwbZorgtoeslagProcess as shells, TreeFellingPermitSubProcess, ZorgtoeslagProvisionalSubProcess, and ZorgtoeslagFinalSubProcess as subprocesses
Imported and user-created processes default to standalone with bpmnProcessId derived from the BPMN <process id="..."> attribute
Process library renders a grouped hierarchical view: shell processes are top-level entries, their subprocesses are indented beneath with a tree connector
SHELL and SUB role badges displayed on process cards for at-a-glance orientation
PostgreSQL process_definitions table stores process_role, called_element, and bpmn_process_id as indexed columns enabling server-side hierarchy queries

sections.title: Schema Versioning
items: schema_version column added to all three PostgreSQL tables (process_definitions, form_schemas, document_templates)
Enables server-side re-seeding of example assets when source files change — all users on all devices receive updates automatically on next connect, without requiring a localStorage reset

sections.title: RIP Phase 1 Process Bundle
items: New deployment bundle for the Regular Infrastructure Projects (RIP) Phase 1 workflow — Project Definition & Preliminary Design Preparation

BPMN process covering the full Phase 1 scope: intake form, intake meeting, intake report, PSU organisation, PSU execution, PSU report, risk file, preliminary design principles, and two approval gateways
RipProjectTypeAssignment DMN determines candidateGroups and assignedRoles from projectType and department; designed for granular RBAC extension without BPMN changes
Seven forms: rip-intake, rip-intake-meeting, rip-intake-report, rip-psu-organize, rip-psu-execution, rip-risk-file, and a reusable rip-approval form shared by both approval gateways
Three document templates bound to process variables: intake report (column 2), PSU report (column 3), and preliminary design principles (column 4)
Bundle deployed to examples/organizations/flevoland/rip-phase1/ alongside the existing Flevoland HR onboarding bundle

sections.title: eDOCS Integration (Stub Mode)
items: New EdocsService wrapping the OpenText eDOCS REST API — connect, ensureWorkspace, uploadDocument, getWorkspaceDocuments, and healthCheck

Stub mode (EDOCS_STUB_MODE=true, default) returns realistic fake responses and logs all calls; transparent to BPMN and routes so the full process can run end-to-end before a live eDOCS server is available
Session token cached after POST /connect; automatically re-authenticated on 401/403

New ExternalTaskWorker polls Operaton using the external task pattern (fetchAndLock) for two topics: rip-edocs-workspace (creates or retrieves the project workspace) and rip-edocs-document (renders and uploads a document to eDOCS)
Worker started inside app.listen() and stopped cleanly on SIGTERM/SIGINT
Four new REST endpoints under /v1/edocs: GET /status, POST /workspaces/ensure, POST /documents, GET /workspaces/:id/documents
New EDOCS_BASE_URL, EDOCS_LIBRARY, EDOCS_USER_ID, EDOCS_PASSWORD, and EDOCS_STUB_MODE environment variables

sections.title: DMN Validator — Interaction Rules
items: INT-005 (orphaned inputData) now only fires in DRDs — models with more than one decision or at least one informationRequirement element; single-decision standalone DMNs no longer produce false-positive warnings for their inputData contract declarations

New INT-007 warning: inputExpression variable has no matching top-level inputData declaration — catches the missing inputData elements that cause the CPSV Editor to generate an empty request body on deploy

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Form Editor — Save now correctly persists the current schema; previously the destructured return value of saveSchema() was undefined (form-js 1.20.x returns the schema object directly, not wrapped in { schema }), which caused undefined to be written to localStorage and the active form to disappear on the next render
Form Editor — Export .form now correctly writes the full schema to the downloaded file for the same reason

Form Editor — Vite dedupe config added for preact/preact/hooks/preact/compat to prevent duplicate Preact instances when npm resolves bpmn-io packages; fixes TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'context') that broke the form canvas after package updates

sections.title: Known Issues
items: Form Editor — Typing in a properties panel field (e.g. label, key) loses focus after the first character; this is caused by Preact re-rendering the properties panel internally on every change event inside form-js 1.20.x and is an upstream issue to be resolved in a future release

sections.title: Import from File
items: Import .bpmn files directly into the BPMN Modeler via the Upload button in the process list header
Import .form files directly into the Form Editor via the Upload button in the form list header
Import .document files directly into the Document Composer via the Upload button in the document list header
Imported BPMN processes derive their name from the process element's name attribute in the XML, falling back to the filename
Imported forms derive their name from the schema id field, falling back to the filename
Imported documents receive a fresh id and timestamps on import to avoid collisions with existing templates
All imported items open immediately in their respective editor and are persisted to localStorage

sections.title: Document Composer
items: New Document Composer view for authoring formal government decision documents (beschikkingen)
Fixed-zone document layout: Letterhead, Contact Information, Reference, Body, Closing, Sign-off, and optional Annex
Five block types: rich text (TipTap editor with bold, italic, headings, lists), variable placeholder, image, separator, and spacer
Drag blocks from the Content library onto any zone; reorder or move blocks across zones by dragging
Image library tab fetches assets directly from the active TriplyDB dataset
Documents stored in localStorage with create, rename, delete, and Save as… actions
Export document template as a .document JSON file
Read-only example document pre-loaded: Kapvergunning Beschikking (AwbShellProcess)

sections.title: Variable Bindings
items: Bindings panel links {{placeholder}} tokens in document text to Operaton process variable keys
Discover Variables button queries Operaton history API for all variables used in a given process definition key
Discovered variables shown as clickable chips with type labels (String, Boolean, Double, etc.) for one-click binding creation
Bindings declare source as either process variable or DMN output for audit traceability

sections.title: BPMN Modeler Integration
items: Document Template selector injected into the BPMN properties panel for UserTask elements
Selecting a document template writes ronl:documentRef to the BPMN XML using a custom RONL moddleDescriptor (ronlModdleDescriptor.json)
Purple badge on UserTask canvas elements confirms a document template is linked
Distinct from the existing green form badge and amber DMN badge

sections.title: Deploy Bundle
items: Deploy modal now resolves ronl:documentRef attributes across main BPMN and all subprocess BPMNs
Matched document templates included in the Operaton deployment bundle as .document JSON files alongside .bpmn and .form resources
Resource preview in the deploy modal lists .document files with a purple icon
Backend POST /api/dmns/process/deploy extended to accept and append document templates as multipart resources

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Fixed Task_Phase6_Notify and Task_RequestMissingInfo appearing pre-claimed in the caseworker dashboard — camunda:assignee="demo" removed, camunda:candidateGroups="caseworker" added to both tasks

sections.title: Internal
items: Example .bpmn and .form files moved to public/examples/flevoland/ as the single source of truth — inline schemas removed from bpmnTemplates.ts and FormEditor.tsx
Added example version registry (exampleVersions.ts) — incrementing a version number now pushes updated example files to existing users on next page load without requiring a localStorage reset

sections.title: Form Editor
items: New Form Editor view using @bpmn-io/form-js — create and edit Camunda Forms (schemaVersion 16) directly in the application
Form list panel with create, rename, delete and status badges (EXAMPLE / WIP)
Three built-in example forms: Kapvergunning Start (citizen-facing), Tree Felling Review (caseworker), AWB Notify Applicant (caseworker)
Export individual forms as .form JSON files compatible with Camunda Modeler and Operaton
Forms stored in localStorage and available immediately to the BPMN Modeler

sections.title: BPMN Modeler — Form Integration
items: Link to Form selector in the properties panel for UserTask and StartEvent elements
Selecting a form writes camunda:formRef and camunda:formRefBinding="latest" to the BPMN XML
Green badges on UserTask and StartEvent elements when a form is linked (camunda:formRef present)
DmnTemplateSelector now pre-selects the linked DMN when a BusinessRuleTask is selected (was always empty)

sections.title: BPMN Modeler — One-Click Deploy
items: Deploy button opens a modal listing all resources to be bundled: main BPMN, subprocess BPMNs (calledElement resolution), and linked .form files
All resources deployed in a single multipart POST to Operaton — camunda:formRef resolves at runtime because BPMN and forms share the same deployment ID
Configurable REST endpoint field pre-filled with VITE_OPERATON_BASE_URL so deployments can target any Operaton instance
Optional username and password fields for instances requiring HTTP Basic Auth
Deploy button disabled after a successful deployment to prevent accidental re-deploy

sections.title: Backend — Process Deploy Endpoint
items: POST /api/dmns/process/deploy — deploys BPMN + subprocess BPMNs + Camunda Forms in one multipart request to Operaton
Each resource appended with its filename as the multipart field name, matching Camunda Modeler behaviour
Supports custom Operaton URL and HTTP Basic Auth credentials per request

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Fixed 'Missing 1 required input(s)' error for optional Date inputs (e.g. overlijdensdatum) with a null test value
Fill with test data now explicitly sets Date inputs to null when no schema:value triple exists in RDF, registering the key in state so validation no longer flags it as absent
Validator now treats Date inputs without a value the same as Boolean — a null/empty date is semantically valid and no longer blocks chain execution

sections.title: DMN Validator
items: New dedicated DMN Validator view accessible via the shield icon in the sidebar
Validates DMN files against five syntactic layers: Base DMN, Business Rules, Execution Rules, Interaction Rules, and Content
Multi-file support — drop any number of .dmn or .xml files to validate and compare side-by-side
Drop zone stays permanently visible to add more files without clearing existing results
Each file gets its own independently scrollable card with its own Validate button
'Validate all' button in the header validates all loaded files in one click
Collapsible layer sections per file show issue counts (E/W/I badges) at a glance
Validation state is preserved when navigating to other views and returning

sections.title: Validation Layers
items: Base DMN: XML well-formedness, root element check, DMN namespace detection (1.1/1.2/1.3), required <definitions> attributes, presence of at least one <decision>
Business Rules: hitPolicy enum validation, inputExpression and output typeRef presence and known FEEL types, rule entry count consistency
Execution Rules: CPRMV extension attribute validation — rulesetType, ruleType, confidence enums, ISO date format (YYYY-MM-DD), BWB ID format, temporal-period completeness
Interaction Rules: informationRequirement href resolution, orphaned inputData detection, variable name consistency across DRD wiring
Content: non-empty CPRMV descriptive attributes, variable typeRef presence, non-empty textAnnotation content

sections.title: Backend
items: New POST /v1/dmns/validate endpoint — unauthenticated, accepts DMN XML as a string, returns structured layer results
Validation powered by libxmljs2 for XML parsing and XPath-based DOM traversal across all five layers
Each issue carries a severity (error/warning/info), a typed code (BASE-*, BIZ-*, EXEC-*, INT-*, CON-*), a message, and an optional element location

sections.title: Vendor Service Integration
items: Integrated RONL Ontology v1.0 vendor vocabulary (ronl:VendorService, ronl:basedOn, ronl:implementedBy)
Visual vendor badge system showing count of commercial implementations available for each DMN
Blue vendor badges with implementation count displayed on DMN cards in both Available DMNs list and Chain Composer
Click vendor badges to open detailed modal with provider information, contact details, and service URLs
Vendor count automatically fetched and cached alongside DMN metadata from TriplyDB
Defensive rendering: vendor badges only show when count > 0, no '0' badges displayed
Support for multiple vendor implementations per reference DMN with proper deduplication

sections.title: Backend Vendor Service
items: New vendor service with SPARQL queries supporting RONL vendor vocabulary schema
Deduplication using SAMPLE() aggregation with GROUP BY to handle multiple language tags and blank nodes
API endpoints: GET /v1/vendors (all vendors) and GET /v1/vendors/dmn/:identifier (vendors for specific DMN)
Automatic vendor logo resolution from TriplyDB assets with fallback handling
Vendor count aggregation integrated into DMN queries for efficient single-request data fetching
Support for schema:provider, schema:contactPoint, ronl:implementedBy, and full vendor metadata

sections.title: Vendor Details Modal
items: Comprehensive vendor modal displaying provider name, logo, homepage, and platform (e.g., Blueriq)
License type badges: Commercial, Open Source, Free with color-coded styling
Access type indicators: IAM Required, Public Access, API Key Required
Contact information: name, email (mailto: link), telephone (tel: link) with icons
Direct service URL links to access vendor implementations with external link indicators
Description field showing vendor-specific implementation details in Dutch
Responsive modal design with smooth animations and proper z-index stacking

sections.title: Badge System Enhancements
items: Standardized badge ordering across interface: 1) Validation 2) Vendor 3) DRD 4) Close button
Close button styling improved with white background, border, and red hover state for better visibility
Trash icon properly inherits red color on hover using Tailwind group modifier pattern
Vendor badges use blue color scheme (bg-blue-600) to distinguish from validation badges
Compact badge mode for list views, expanded mode for detailed cards
Event propagation handling: clicking vendor badge doesn't trigger drag operations

sections.title: Type Safety & Data Model
items: New TypeScript interfaces: VendorService, VendorOrganization, VendorContact in vendor.types.ts
Extended DmnModel with optional vendorCount field for seamless integration
Type-safe vendor modal props with proper TypeScript inference throughout component tree
Endpoint parameter properly threaded through component hierarchy (App → ChainBuilder → ChainComposer/DmnList)
Eliminated hardcoded endpoints in favor of prop-based endpoint management

sections.title: User Experience Improvements
items: Vendor badges appear in Available DMNs list enabling discovery before adding to chain
Hover tooltips on vendor badges show implementation count ('1 vendor implementation available')
Loading states in vendor modal with spinner and 'Loading vendor services...' message
Empty state handling: 'No vendor implementations found' with building icon when no vendors exist
Error handling with clear error messages when vendor service fetch fails

sections.title: DMN Validation & Governance System
items: Integrated RONL Ontology v1.0 governance vocabulary for DMN validation metadata
Visual badge system distinguishing validated, in-review, and non-validated decision models
Emerald green 'Gevalideerd' badge for officially validated DMNs by competent authorities
Amber 'In Review' badge for DMNs currently under validation process
Badges display validating organization name (e.g., Sociale Verzekeringsbank, SZW)
Validation dates shown in Dutch format (14 feb 2026) with full details on hover
Badges appear in both Available DMNs list and Chain Composer dropped cards
Non-validated DMNs show no badge, maintaining clean, uncluttered interface by default

sections.title: Backend SPARQL Integration
items: Enhanced SPARQL query with UNION support for backward compatibility with legacy namespaces
Queries both old (ronl: <.../termen/>) and new (ronl-gov: <.../ontology#>) vocabularies
Automatic resolution of validating organization names via skos:prefLabel lookup
Fetches ronl:validationStatus, ronl:validatedBy, ronl:validatedAt, ronl:validationNote from TriplyDB
Graceful handling of missing validation metadata using OPTIONAL SPARQL blocks
5-minute caching per endpoint for optimal performance with validation data

sections.title: User Experience & Accessibility
items: WCAG AA compliant color contrast for validation badges (emerald 600, amber 500)
Icon + text badges (not color-only) for accessibility and visual clarity
Hover tooltips display full validation details: organization, date, and notes
Compact badge mode in DMN list (icon + short label), expanded mode in cards
Screen reader friendly with semantic HTML and proper ARIA labels
Responsive design: badges adapt to small screens by hiding text, showing icon only
Dutch language labels: 'Gevalideerd' and 'In Review' for localized user experience

sections.title: Data Model Extensions
items: Extended DmnModel interface with validationStatus, validatedBy, validatedByName, validatedAt, validationNote fields
TypeScript type safety for validation status: 'validated' | 'in-review' | 'not-validated'
Frontend and backend type definitions synchronized for end-to-end type safety
Validation metadata flows through: TriplyDB → Backend SPARQL → Frontend State → UI Components

sections.title: Template System Enhancement
items: Enhanced template system to support both DRD and sequential chain templates with distinct 'type' field
Added visual indicators: 🎯 purple badge for DRD templates, ⛓️ amber badge for sequential templates
Save button automatically detects chain type (DRD vs sequential) and adjusts behavior accordingly
DRD templates deploy to Operaton and store deployment ID, sequential templates save directly to localStorage
Template list clearly shows type badges enabling users to distinguish execution modes at a glance
Modal titles dynamically update: 'Save as DRD Template' vs 'Save as Sequential Template'
Auto-detection uses validation state to determine if chain is DRD-compatible or requires sequential execution

sections.title: Semantic Chain Validation
items: Improved semantic link detection with proper React dependency management for reliable validation
Added semanticLinks to validation useEffect dependency array ensuring re-validation when links load
Validation now correctly distinguishes between exact identifier matches (DRD-compatible) and semantic matches (sequential-only)
Real-time detection of semantic variable links with clear warning messages: '⚠️ Sequential execution required (semantic links)'
Console logging shows clear validation status: '✓ DRD' or '⚠️ Sequential' with semantic match counts

sections.title: UX Improvements
items: Unified button layout with three equal-width actions: Execute | Save | Export for consistent interface
Button text dynamically updates based on chain type: 'Save as DRD' vs 'Save Template'
Loading states show appropriate messages: 'Deploying...' for DRDs, 'Saving...' for sequential chains
Export button integrated seamlessly into three-button layout replacing previous inconsistent positioning
Semantic chain warning badges appear below action buttons with amber color scheme for clear visibility

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Fixed validation crash when dragging DMNs into chain composer due to null reference errors
Added optional chaining (validation?.isValid) throughout component preventing crashes during initial composition
Fixed boolean input validation incorrectly treating unchecked checkboxes as missing inputs
Updated validation logic to recognize unchecked boolean inputs as valid with default false value
Fixed DRD deployment API parameter: changed 'templateName' to 'deploymentName' matching backend expectations

sections.title: DRD Card Display & UX Improvements
